key_insight: IMCBench shows that multimodal medical LLMs can describe images well yet still give unsafe or uncertain clinical guidance, so performance must be judged beyond accuracy alone.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark highlights why image-grounded, multi-turn evaluation is important for clinical decision support and triage tools that may influence patient-facing guidance.
method: Built IMCBench using real public clinical images plus synthetic patient profiles for multi-turn medical conversations.
Evaluated eight frontier multimodal models across safety, accuracy, and appropriate uncertainty using 1–5 LLM-as-Jury scoring calibrated to clinician annotations.
Ran ablations to test the impact of removing visual input and EHR context on model safety.
evidence_signal: Claude Opus 4.6 had the highest overall score (3.61), followed by Claude Sonnet 4.6 (3.30) and GPT-5.2 (3.29); safety dropped when visual input or EHR context was removed, and weakened for malignant and rare cases.
watch_item: The benchmark relies on synthetic patient profiles and LLM-as-Jury scoring, so results may not fully capture real-world clinical complexity or deployment risk.
paper_title: IMCBench: A benchmark for multimodal LLMs in Image-grounded Medical Conversations
